examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}が{俄然|がぜん}{面白|おもしろ}くなった。
そのニュースで{俄然|がぜん}やる{気|き}が{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: That news suddenly made me feel motivated.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{証拠|しょうこ}が{見|み}つかり、{捜査|そうさ}は{俄然|がぜん}{活気|かっき}を{帯|お}びた。
examples.english: New evidence was found, and the investigation suddenly picked up momentum.

notes:
An adverb indicating a sudden and dramatic change, typically for the better or toward greater intensity. Unlike {突然|とつぜん}, which simply marks an abrupt event, {俄然|がぜん} implies that a situation has transformed noticeably and often carries a sense of heightened energy or interest.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {俄然|がぜん}やる{気|き}が{出|で}る: suddenly feel motivated
- {俄然|がぜん}{面白|おもしろ}くなる: suddenly become interesting
- {俄然|がぜん}{注目|ちゅうもく}を{集|あつ}める: suddenly attract attention
- {俄然|がぜん}{有利|ゆうり}になる: suddenly become advantageous

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {突然|とつぜん}: suddenly — neutral, marks any abrupt event
- {急|きゅう}に: suddenly, quickly — more colloquial
- にわかに: suddenly — literary, often implies an unexpected shift
